newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Three killed, 200 hurt in Bangladesh strike.
newsitem.headline: Three killed, 200 hurt in Bangladesh strike.

text.p: Three people were killed and nearly 200 injured in sporadic violence in Bangladesh during a general strike called by the main opposition party, newspapers reported on Monday.

Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader, former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, called Sunday's strike in her first attempt to destabilise the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, who took office last June.

The newspapers, quoting witnesses and police, said an officer of the Bangladesh Naval Academy, Fazlul Karim, was shot dead by BNP activists in the southern district of Laxmipur after they failed to find his son, a student leader of the ruling Awami League.
One man died of suffocation in the northern district of Natore where strike supporters set fire to a jute warehouse, local officials told reporters.
Another person died when a passenger coach of a train ran off the tracks, which had been damaged by suspected strike enforcers, near Chittagong port.
Nearly 200 people were injured in strike-related violence across the country, the press reports said.
Police said they detained more than 150 activists during the eight-hour strike, which shut businesses and kept transport off the roads.

The BNP said the strike was to protest what it viewed as the government's failure to provide basic needs for people in this poor nation and against Hasina's warmer ties with India, which the BNP sees as a plot to surrender Bangladeshi sovereignty.
